roz-mytheme-job.name: Job
roz-mytheme-job.description: The whole biblical movement: the councils Job never hears, the losses, the friends' seven-day silence and three rounds of explanation, wisdom's place, the oath, Elihu, the two whirlwind speeches with their creatures, and the return through intercession and the named daughters — first losses retained.

scenes.name: The councils Job never hears
scenes.character: The reader is shown what Job and his friends are not: the wager precedes the suffering, and the account that suffering proves wrongdoing will confront a man whose integrity the opening affirmed.

entities.name: the council — sons of God presenting; Satan among them
Job — upright; sacrifices toward a fault he has not witnessed
the permission — what Job has, not his person; then his flesh, life spared

text.title: The councils Job never hears
text.italic: The narrative demonstrates an asymmetry of knowledge running through the whole encounter: the reader watches servants and children die in a test addressed to someone else's fidelity.

text.body: In Uz, Job's uprightness has a household — seven sons, three daughters, livestock, servants, feasts; his sacrifices reach toward a fault he has not witnessed. When the sons of God present themselves, Satan comes among them. The LORD points to Job's integrity; Satan answers: "Doth Job fear God for nought?" Permission reaches what Job has, not his person. The losses arrive through messengers, each still speaking when the next comes:

fire, Chaldeans, the great wind on the children's feast house. Job worships; he has not charged God foolishly — the council stays undisclosed to him. The second council shifts the bargain to his body; sores cover him; his wife urges curse and die; he receives evil too. The friends arrive and sit seven days in silence — the companionship their later failure must be read against.
Occurrences: the two councils (#0); the four messengers and the wind (#0); the potsherd and ashes (#0); the wife's words (#0); the seven-day silence (#0, recalled at #1).

scenes.name: The three rounds: comfort becoming accusation
scenes.character: Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar explain; Job answers, protests, and asks for a hearing — the explanation begins to add an injury of its own.

entities.name: Eliphaz — the innocent do not perish; affliction as chastening
Bildad — divine justice; the children's death explained
Zophar — God exacts less than your iniquity deserves
Job — miserable comforters; "he is not a man as I am"; no daysman
the engraving — "written, engraved with iron and lead, cut into rock" (19:23–24)
the prosperous wicked — evidence against the friends' rule (ch. 21)

text.title: The three rounds: comfort becoming accusation
text.italic: The friends' certainty embodies the protected account: contradiction is received as further evidence of the judged person's defect.

text.body: Job breaks the silence cursing the day of his birth — not the curse Satan predicted. Eliphaz begins from Job's former strength and the innocency question; Job answers flesh-not-stone, asks the pity a friend owes, compares them to brooks failing caravans. Bildad insists on divine justice — the children's death explicable through transgression; Job answers that no daysman lays a hand on them both. Zophar intensifies the

accusation; Job replies that wisdom is not their possession. Second round: his words become evidence; he wants them preserved — written, engraved with iron and lead, cut into rock — with the living redeemer. Third: Eliphaz alleges cruelties; chapter 24 widens the witness to workers hungry while handling food. The poem keeps its complexity; Zophar gets no third speech.
Occurrences: the brooks simile (#1); the daysman (#1); the iron-and-lead engraving (#1); the prosperous wicked (#1); the missing third Zophar speech (#1).

scenes.name: Chapter 28 — where wisdom's place is not
scenes.character: Human skill reaches the earth's hidden interior; wisdom's place is not found by the same achievement. "The fear of the Lord, that is wisdom."

entities.name: the miner's shafts — hidden ore brought to light
the channels cut through rock; water restrained
Abaddon and Death — have heard the report thereof with their ears
wisdom's place — known to God; wind, water, rain and thunder exceed the miner's reach

text.title: Chapter 28 — where wisdom's place is not
text.italic: The chapter honours discovery while asking after a knowledge extraction cannot secure — depth and sea cannot supply it; gold cannot purchase it.

text.body: Between the disputed judgments and the final oath, chapter 28 follows human skill underground: shafts opened, hidden ore brought to light, channels cut through rock, water restrained. The earth that feeds them has another interior their labour can reach. Wisdom's place does not become available by the same achievement: the deep says, It is not in me; the sea says, It is not with me; gold and

precious stones cannot be given for it. Destruction and death have heard the report with their ears. God knows the place — an ordering of wind, water, rain and thunder beyond the miner's reach. The chapter gives reverence and departing from evil as the human relation to wisdom. No character named Sophia enters this scene.
Occurrences: the mining shafts and ore (#2); Abaddon and Death's report (#2); the fear of the Lord as wisdom (#2).

scenes.name: The oath and Elihu
scenes.character: Job binds his claim to contestable particulars and asks for the adversary's written charge; Elihu changes the proposed work of suffering yet still defends justice.

entities.name: the oath of ch. 31 — desire, servants, the widow and orphan, the stranger, the enemy; "let thine answer be a scroll"
the written charge — carried on the shoulder, as a crown
Elihu — angry at both sides; spirit over seniority; belly like wine
the weather gathering — clouds, rain, frost, light, thunder (36–37)

text.title: The oath and Elihu
text.italic: The oath names the relations under which innocence could be examined; Elihu's intervention must be heard in tension — the offered explanation is more various, yet justice is again defended at the sufferer's expense.

text.body: Job remembers his public righteousness with concrete recipients — poor, fatherless, widow, blind, lame — and chapter 30 records the inversion: those he once despised now mock him, his harsh distinctions preserved. The oath of chapter 31 binds his claim to contestable particulars: desire, adultery, servants, hunger, nakedness, the stranger's lodging; against contempt for a servant's cause he invokes their common making in the womb. He asks for the

Almighty's answer and the adversary's written charge, carried on his shoulder and as a crown. Elihu takes six chapters: angry at Job's self-justification and at condemnation without answer; understanding through spirit rather than seniority; suffering as instruction — yet 34–35 bring Job's speech under fresh judgment. Weather begins to displace the courtroom; Elihu's absence from the named rebuke in 42 certifies none of his claims.

Rain falls where no man lives, satisfying the wilderness — consequential precisely without serving Job's

servant, keep him as a plaything for daughters, sell him among merchants? Weapons are stubble; his breath kindles coals; the boiling sea and luminous wake develop a strength these uses cannot master. text.body: An eye opens upon a world. Something stands forward; something recedes; a face can be approached, a path followed. There is a direction from which these things appear, even when attention belongs wholly to what appears. The eye's condition does not arrive as one more face or obstacle — it is already at work in their appearing. Turning towards it, every disclosure

occurs through a further situation of seeing — a mirror shows the eye, a diagram its structures, another observer an angle unavailable from here. The blindside is the condition that lets a view have a foreground at all. The frame gives it an edge, exclusion productive; the horizon is the field within which anything can come forward, changed by walking and reply. Finitude gives disclosure its positive capacity.

Blue and yellow are known different in one cognition. The dream carries the forgetting: while dreaming, sleep disappears from the experienced situation; waking changes their relation to their condition, not that it never occurred. Recurrence is not captivity: capture begins when the result erases its status as result and circulates as self-originating authority.

scenes.name: A physicist meets his concepts in a dream
scenes.character: Background physics: physical concepts appearing spontaneously in dreams, in a qualitative symbolic sense — received before it is chosen.

text.title: A physicist meets his concepts in a dream
text.italic: The dream sequence demonstrates symbolic description arriving in a mode the dreamer did not consciously choose — and his initial finding of it offensive to scientific habit.

text.body: Pauli's egg dream is a sequence of seven pictures. He introduces "background physics" as physical concepts appearing spontaneously in dreams in a qualitative, symbolic sense — initially offensive to his scientific habits, then an inquiry into the psychic activity of such images and the archetypal background of scientific concepts, explicitly distinguished from a formulated body of scientific truths. Two related dreams fall in an interval

of four days in mid-March, after the Kepler work; the later 60P letter dates the first to 1948 and the essay to June 1948. Göttingen belongs to the companion dream, with the changed hydrogen ground state and brass tones on a metal plate. The egg dream names no city, room or landscape; its space is enacted by arrival, approach and the discovery of something already in the dreamer's hand.
Occurrences: the seven-picture sequence (#0–#3); the mid-March pairing and its retrospective dating (#0); the Göttingen companion dream kept distinct (#0); Fierz's undated typescript (#0).

text.title: Pictures 1–2: the egg laid; the egg divides itself
text.italic: The dream demonstrates plurality made before agency appears: the division occurs without Pauli's reported intervention.

text.body: Picture 1: a woman comes with a bird; the bird lays a large egg. The account gives neither the woman's name nor the bird's species — nothing in the later formula retroactively supplies them a historical identity. The first diagram shows the single egg, its enclosing outline still the form of one thing awaiting what will happen. Picture 2: the egg

divides itself into two. Pauli's grammatical distinction matters — this division occurs without his reported intervention. Two complete egg outlines stand beside one another; they are not described as a good and an evil egg, and no conflict occurs between them. What changes is the field of the image: one has become two while each remains presented as an egg.
Occurrences: the woman and bird's arrival and laying (#1, no further actions); the self-division (#1); the two-whole-eggs result (#1, mirrored consciously at #2).

scenes.character: The dreamer goes closer, finds a blue-shelled egg already held, divides it — and the two miraculously remain whole.

entities.name: picture 3 — the blue-shelled egg in his hand
the marvel — two eggs, not two broken portions

text.title: Pictures 3–4: the egg in his own hand; division that keeps wholeness
text.italic: The scene passes from watching a division to performing one upon what he holds — the event on which his later commentary concentrates.

text.body: Picture 3: Pauli goes closer and notices another egg in his hand, this one with a blue shell. The account does not say he manufactures it or takes it from the first pair; the diagram adds the third beneath the two above, changing the count and the dreamer's position. Picture 4: he divides this last egg into two; they miraculously remain whole, and he now has two

blue-shelled eggs. The source records preservation through division as the marvel: two eggs, not two broken portions requiring an invented repair; no hatching, no discarded shell. The two pairs have related but distinct histories — one from spontaneous change witnessed, one from his recognition and action. Its force would disappear if the four eggs were introduced at once as an emblem with four fixed meanings.
Occurrences: the approach and the noticed egg (#2); the performed division and preserved wholeness (#2); the two origins of the four eggs (#1–#2, retained at #4–#5).

picture 6 — the quotient [cos+i·sin]/[cos−i·sin], modulus one in the denominator
the opposing signs retained in one relation

text.title: Pictures 5–6: four eggs become expressions; the conjugate quotient
text.italic: The dream's organisation changes from four displayed terms into a single relation that retains their opposing signs — an ordinary, well-defined complex-number operation.

text.body: Picture 5: the four eggs change into four mathematical expressions, printed as two rows each holding a cosine term on the left and a sine term on the right. The duplicated terms preserve the paired arrangement while changing the medium of the scene; the picture does not assign each shell colour to a function, so no such assignment is added.

Picture 6: the terms give the quotient with cos(δ/2)+i·sin(δ/2) over cos(δ/2)−i·sin(δ/2) — the cosine the same while the imaginary sine term changes sign; for real δ the denominator has modulus one. The dream's organisation has changed from four displayed terms into a single relation retaining their opposing signs.
Occurrences: the four-eggs-to-expressions transformation (#3, from the four of #1–#2); the conjugate quotient (#3); the retained opposing signs (#3).

text.body: Picture 7: Pauli speaks for the first time in this dream. He identifies the expression with e^{iδ} and names the circle; the formula vanishes and a circle appears. The explanation makes the step explicit: the quotient equals e^{iδ/2} over e^{−iδ/2}, which is e^{iδ} — for a fixed real angle a point on the unit circle; as the angle varies, the circle.

The distinction keeps the operation exact while preserving what Pauli recognises. The account reports neither a return of the woman and bird nor a restart of the first picture; the completion has the history of differentiation and conscious action within it.

text.title: Light entering a made aperture
text.italic: The whole embodies constructing from diaphaneity: composing a work so its originating relation becomes perceptible through the differences of its materials.

text.body: Light enters a room through a window assembled from differently coloured panes. The panes give it determinate passages; the lead holds their boundaries; an image falls into the interior where someone can encounter it. The visible colour carries the work of relations the colour alone cannot display completely. This is Frank Taylor's authored Mytheme of constructing from diaphaneity — no

historical window or sacred programme reconstructed. The originating light has priority over the projected image, yet the viewer encounters the image first and follows its differences back: what is prior in being can be later in recognition. Bimba names the Original order; pratibimba names its determinate display; neither viewer nor maker supplies the Original by finishing the picture.

text.body: The white light carries plenitude: its apparent unity holds the possibility of differentiated colour together with the relations through which the colours belong to one field. Within Taylor's optic this full ordered spectrum figures QL — immanent to the originating light as its harmonic articulation. The pane gives a difference a passage; it does not first create the capacity for difference in a contentless source.

The native theorem spine grounds the relation: the parent phases bearing the positional field in inverse orientations, the First Spanda's source-to-expression and return-to-recognition joined through their interference term. The optical whole makes that fullness and return visible, leaving the equations' derivation in the theorem field. QL's sixfold body and eight-determination traversal remain distinct from the number of panes: none requires a pane to receive a permanent number, tradition or colour.

text.title: Colour acquires a passage; the joins stay visible

text.body: Each pane has a material, density, colour and angle: placement permits some transmission, bends or colours what passes, leaves something obstructed. Removing every difference in pursuit of neutrality would also remove the transformations through which the composition becomes articulate. The original quilt distinguishes the window from an opaque mosaic: the mosaic arranges fragments into a surface image; the window works through transmission and obstruction as well as arrangement.

The lead cames carry the joins — holding neighbouring panes in relation while marking where one passage ends and another begins; in the epistemic construction the seams retain provenance, discontinuity, translation limits, contradiction and changes of register. These figure MEF, whose office C39 defines: a lens changes a question, a permissible inference or an act of judgment while keeping its conditions inspectable.

text.title: The resignation that becomes an address
text.italic: The opening act demonstrates assignment: the inquiry into who may order the field is redirected into an order within that field — "You are Number Six."

text.body: An intelligence agent resigns; before he can carry that decision into another life he is abducted, waking in surroundings resembling his own room — now belonging to the Village. The administration wants the reason for his resignation: it knows much, and seeks cooperation in completing the account. Its visible chief is Number Two; his own designation is Number Six. "Arrival" gives the arrangement material actors: technicians watching, Rover

intercepting escape, Cobb apparently dead, Number Nine's arrangement ending in a remotely controlled helicopter, another man already installed as Number Two. The title exchange compresses the situation — "Who is Number One?" / "You are Number Six." / "I am not a number; I am a free man!" — Two's laughter follows. No comma after "are": the reply assigns the questioner's number; it does not conceal an identity.

text.title: The picture arrives before the pieces
text.italic: The lid embodies the diagnostic: the world approached as though its possible appearances had already been cut by a maker whose picture requires only assembly.

text.body: The puzzle begins with its destination visible. The maker sets out the edges, builds the frame, sorts the remaining pieces by marks promising a place within it; each fit confirms part of the anticipated whole. Yet the finished picture entered the work before the first piece: it supplies the criterion for every later placement. The maker can hesitate over a patch of colour while remaining entirely certain what

counts as completion; the lid decides which differences belong together, which edge is outside, and which apparent anomaly is merely a piece awaiting its correct position. Heidegger's world-picture passages historicise the diagnosis — world grasped as picture and the representer installed as its normative centre belong to one event. text.title: Travel changes what it means to fit
text.italic: The change demonstrates itself: pieces become local charts whose edges mark limits of usable description, and neighbours overlap rather than merely meet along a cut.

text.body: The puzzle travels into the world it claims to depict. Its maker encounters a turn the flat arrangement cannot preserve, a continuation beyond an edge, a view distorting with position. At first the assembly absorbs it as traveller's error — another piece still judged under the same criterion. The change: the maker records how a view was made: from where, across which region, under what projection, with which

omissions. Pieces become local charts; their edges mark limits of usable description; neighbours overlap rather than merely meet. Within an overlap the maker explains how a position here appears there; a difference between reports can disclose a change of coordinates, a difference of measurement, or an unresolved disagreement. The seam becomes operative, and an atlas can be worked: enter a chart, cross an overlap, learn what changed, return routed.

text.kicker: #2 · the manifold-atlas matheme (Derived in its home; the crossing Offered)
text.title: A crossing has a rule — the circle's two charts
text.italic: The example demonstrates local pictures disagreeing in written values while agreeing in what those values describe — the overlap and transformation explain the agreement.

text.body: The mathematical witness is Offered; the constructions keep the Derived standing of their matheme homes. Two charts cover the circle by omitting opposite poles. At the point (x,y)=(3/5,4/5), their coordinates are u=3 and v=1/3; on the overlap the rule is v=1/u. The reports differ numerically because they use different coordinates; the declared transformation identifies their common point. Height is 4/5 in either account. Even motion must be

transformed: when du/dt=2 at this point, dv/dt=−2/9, and both descriptions give the same change of height — giving both coordinate velocities the number two would change the motion described. Conversely, when the inverse is missing, the common domain absent, or regularity fails, no conclusion follows. Compact circle, sphere and torus admit no single global chart into an open Euclidean domain of the same dimension; compactness gives the obstruction.

text.kicker: #0 · native QL/Mytheme register; authored whole-image recovery; quilt §§3–6 toroidal correction
text.title: The snake bends until its head meets its tail
text.italic: The trickster embodies the round presented as the whole truth of the creature — the whole image is toroidal, and its wholeness keeps the opening around which it takes form.

text.body: The snake bends until its head meets its tail; hunger moves along a relation in which eater and eaten belong to one life. This is the whole image in Taylor's native register: the uroboros is toroidal, and its wholeness keeps the opening. The trickster wears the circle as costume: head and tail appear to complete a circumference, and that visible completion offers itself as the whole truth. Two consequences follow

the mouth — assimilation lets what enters change the life that receives it; devouring closure takes everything into an order whose continuation must leave that order untouched. In the Saturnine image the gut is blocked: consumption arrests the generation it claims to sustain. Human-amplified: yes for the toroidal whole, circle/sphere trickster, metabolic fork, Eden relation and complete eightfold recapitulation in the authored quilt.

text.title: Position and opposition

A circle is real as a circle; the error begins when its completeness answers for the living whole. The quilt sharpens this through (-1)+(+1)=0 — the cancelling zero takes a terminated account's office; arithmetic exact, its mythemic work the cost felt. Opposition restores head and tail

as oriented terms: the head reaches, the tail is reached; hunger gives the orientation urgency. Neumann's pp.27–35 sequence follows nourishment through hunger, ingestion, excretion and self-formation. The two Ones preserve what the costume conceals: 0 as One, Self-Identity; 1 as All, Self-Difference — neither office can swallow the other. The hungry head becomes tyrannical at the crossing from local appetite to exhaustive authority (A12).
